title: Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365: which settings does each user's Office get?
summary: Hold: the page omits exceptions that affect enforcement and availability. Some privacy policies apply without restarting Office, disabling OneDrive creation prevents Pages and Notebooks creation regardless of this policy, and Microsoft 365 Apps for business does receive privacy-control policies.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy enforces Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise settings on a user's device even if it is unmanaged.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365 lets you enforce policy settings for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on a user's device, even if the device isn't domain joined or otherwise managed.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Policy settings follow the signed-in user rather than the machine.
claims.quote: When a user signs into Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise on a device, the policy settings roam to that device.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy is managed in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at config.office.com.
claims.quote: To create or edit policy configurations you must sign into the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: An administrator creates a policy configuration containing a name, a scope and chosen policy settings.
claims.quote: On the Start with the basics page, enter a name (required) and a description (optional), then select Next. On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.

claims.claim: Scope choices are all users, specific Microsoft Entra groups, or anonymous Office for the web users.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Click-to-Run checks in regularly for policies pertaining to the signed-in user.
claims.quote: The Click-to-Run service used by Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise checks in with the Cloud Policy service regularly to see if there are any policies that pertain to the signed in user.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Policies retrieved at check-in take effect the next time the user opens an Office app.
claims.quote: If there are, then the appropriate policies are applied and take effect the next time the user opens an Office app, such as Word or Excel.

claims.where: What it is: What it governs
claims.claim: Settings are available on Windows, macOS, iOS and Android, but not every setting is available on every operating system.
claims.quote: Policy settings are available for devices running Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android, although not all policy settings are available for all operating systems.

claims.where: What it is: What it governs
claims.claim: Some Cloud Policy settings also apply to Office for the web and Loop.
claims.quote: You can also enforce some policy settings for Office for the web and Loop, both for guests who are signed in and for users who access documents anonymously.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Users, not devices
claims.claim: Only user-based policies are available and policies apply only to user objects, not computers.
claims.quote: Only user-based policy settings are available. Computer-based policy settings aren't available. Policies only apply to user objects.

claims.where: What it is: What it governs
claims.claim: New user-based Office settings are added automatically without downloading updated ADMX/ADML files.
claims.quote: As new user-based policy settings are made available for Office, Cloud Policy automatically adds them. There's no need to download updated Administrative Templates files (ADMX/ADML).

claims.claim: The TCM reference describes 20 Copilot resources as Cloud Policy settings.
claims.quote: The 20 Copilot resources are Office Cloud Policy Service (OCPS) settings.

claims.where: What it is: Copilot settings; controls[2].governs
claims.claim: Administrators control Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks creation and use through Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: IT administrators can control creation and use of Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks through Cloud Policy settings.

claims.claim: New Outlook supplies a non-Copilot example of Cloud Policy controls.
claims.quote: Disable contact support is configured via Cloud Policy for a Microsoft 365 organization from the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, specifically on the Office Policies page.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/manage/policy-management to sources for the non-Copilot Outlook example; the linked wiki briefing is not evidence.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents the Copilot Pages and Notebooks creation setting as Enabled by default.
claims.quote: | Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks creation | Cloud Policy: Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks | Enabled |

claims.claim: Not configured leaves creation and integration available, so a tenant that never sets the policy leaves the feature open to users.
claims.quote: If your organization disabled the creation of OneDrive, regardless of the setting noted here, these people in your organization can't create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks.
claims.fix: Replace the final two sentences of the first Why it matters paragraph with: 'Not configured leaves creation and integration available, except that users for whom the organisation has disabled OneDrive creation cannot create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks, regardless of this policy.'

claims.claim: Cloud Policy supports most Microsoft 365 subscription plans that include Microsoft 365 Apps.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy supports most Microsoft 365 subscription plans that include Microsoft 365 Apps.

claims.claim: Microsoft tells administrators to check licensing documentation for specific requirements.
claims.quote: Check your licensing documentation for specific requirements.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet is not supported.
claims.quote: The following plans are not supported: Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet

claims.claim: User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID and have a supported license assigned.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits: Users, not devices
claims.claim: Users must have a supported licence assigned to receive policies.
claims.quote: User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID and have a supported license assigned.

claims.claim: The overview page publishes no separate price or meter for Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Cloud Policy service health reporting retirement pricing meter cost'; '"Cloud Policy" "price" "licensing"'. Read https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy in full; it lists licensing requirements but no separate price or meter.

claims.claim: The TCM reference says Copilot Notebooks also require a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks also require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Wrong product edition
claims.claim: Policy configurations cannot apply to volume licensed Click-to-Run Office such as Office LTSC Professional Plus 2021 or Office Standard 2019.
claims.quote: A policy configuration can't be applied to volume licensed versions of Office that use Click-to-Run, such as Office LTSC Professional Plus 2021 or Office Standard 2019.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Wrong product edition
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Apps for business supports only privacy-control policy settings.
claims.quote: You can create a policy configuration for Microsoft 365 Apps for business, but only policy settings related to privacy controls are supported.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Wrong product edition
claims.claim: The concluding advice says to expect no effect on the clients just named, including Microsoft 365 Apps for business.
claims.quote: For Microsoft 365 Apps for business, only privacy-control settings are supported. Expect no effect on those clients.
claims.fix: Remove 'Expect no effect on those clients.' It conflicts with both the preceding sentence and the overview's documented support for privacy controls in Microsoft 365 Apps for business.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Users, not devices
claims.claim: Device objects in targeted groups are ignored.
claims.quote: A group might contain both device objects and user objects, but the device objects are ignored.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Conflicting groups
claims.claim: The highest-priority configuration resolves conflicting settings for users belonging to several targeted groups.
claims.quote: If the user is a member of multiple Microsoft Entra groups with conflicting policy settings, priority is used to determine which policy setting is applied. The highest priority is applied

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Conflicting groups
claims.claim: Priority 0 is the highest assignable priority.
claims.quote: The highest priority is applied, with "0" being the highest priority that you can assign.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Delay and restart
claims.claim: Settings apply only when the Office app restarts.
claims.quote: If the primary account is switched, most of the policies assigned to that account will not apply until the Office apps are restarted. Some policies related to privacy controls will apply without restarting any Office apps.
claims.fix: Replace 'Settings apply only when the Office app restarts.' with 'Office policy changes generally require an app restart, but some privacy-control policies apply without restarting Office apps.' In Why it matters replace 'and an app restart' with 'and generally an app restart, with exceptions for some privacy-control policies'.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Delay and restart; Why it matters
claims.claim: On Windows, only the primary signed-in account's policies apply.
claims.quote: For Windows devices, policies are enforced based on the primary user that is signed into Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise. If there are multiple accounts signed in, only policies for the primary account are applied.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Delay and restart; What to check
claims.claim: The Copilot Pages documentation allows up to 90 minutes for a change where policy configurations already existed.
claims.quote: If there were existing policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 90 minutes to be reflected.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Delay and restart; What to check
claims.claim: The Copilot Pages documentation allows up to 24 hours for a change where no policy configurations existed.
claims.quote: If there were no policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 24 hours to be reflected.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Overrides Group Policy
claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings take precedence over Group Policy on Windows Server.
claims.quote: policy settings implemented by using Cloud Policy take precedence over policy settings implemented by using Group Policy on Windows Server

claims.where: Risks and limits: Overrides Group Policy
claims.claim: Cloud Policy settings take precedence over preference and locally applied policy settings.
claims.quote: taking precedence over preference settings or locally applied policy settings.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No health view
claims.claim: Cloud Policy's health status feature was retired in March 2022.
claims.quote: The health status feature was retired in the second half of March 2022.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No health view; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft gives no date for planned replacement advanced health reporting and compliance monitoring.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Cloud Policy" "health status" "reporting"'. Read https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy: 'In the future (no known date at this time), we plan to provide advanced health reporting and compliance monitoring features for Cloud Policy.'

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risks and limits: Scripting is narrow; Open questions
claims.claim: TCM supports these Copilot Cloud Policy settings only in tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Scripting is narrow
claims.claim: Configuring the same setting in any group-level policy makes TCM monitoring and applyOnce fail for that resource.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risks and limits: Scripting is narrow
claims.claim: The documented TCM Copilot Graph route is preview and uses beta APIs.
claims.quote: This article lists the Copilot resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: Devices require access to Microsoft's listed endpoints, including *.config.office.com for commercial and GCC.
claims.quote: Devices running Microsoft 365 Apps require access to the following endpoints: Commercial and GCC | Microsoft 365 Apps admin center | - login.live.com - *.office.com - *.office.net - *.config.office.com - *.config.office.net

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator can manage Cloud Policy and is the recommended role.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended) | This role can manage Office apps cloud services, including policy and settings management

claims.claim: Security Administrator is a supported role for accessing and managing Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: You can use the following built-in Microsoft Entra roles for accessing and managing the feature: Security Administrator

claims.claim: Global Administrator is a supported role for managing Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Global Administrator | This role can manage all aspects of Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft services that use Microsoft Entra identities.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in user role for Copilot TCM remediation and applyOnce.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: The overview directs commercial and US Government customers to config.office.com.
claims.quote: Commercial and US Government customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at https://config.office.com

claims.claim: Cloud Policy is also accessible in the Microsoft Intune admin center under Apps > Policy > Policies for Office apps.
claims.quote: or directly in the Microsoft Intune admin center, under Apps > Policy > Policies for Office apps.

claims.claim: GCC High and DoD have separate admin center addresses in the overview.
claims.quote: US Government Community (GCC) High customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at https://config.office365.us. Department of Defense (DoD) customers can access the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at https://config.apps.mil

claims.claim: Cloud Policy supports Microsoft Purview auditing.
claims.quote: Cloud Policy service supports the Microsoft Purview auditing solutions.

claims.claim: When auditing is enabled, policy configuration creation is tracked.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as the creation, deletion, modification of policy configurations, changes to configured policy settings, and adjustments to priority order are tracked.

claims.claim: When auditing is enabled, policy configuration deletion is tracked.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as the creation, deletion, modification of policy configurations, changes to configured policy settings, and adjustments to priority order are tracked.

claims.claim: When auditing is enabled, policy configuration modification is tracked.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as the creation, deletion, modification of policy configurations, changes to configured policy settings, and adjustments to priority order are tracked.

claims.claim: When auditing is enabled, priority-order changes are tracked.
claims.quote: When auditing is enabled, events such as the creation, deletion, modification of policy configurations, changes to configured policy settings, and adjustments to priority order are tracked.

claims.claim: CreatedPolicyConfig is the audit operation for a newly created policy configuration.
claims.quote: | Created policy configuration | CreatedPolicyConfig | A new policy configuration was created. |

claims.claim: UpdatedPolicyConfig identifies updates to an existing policy configuration.
claims.quote: | Updated policy configuration | UpdatedPolicyConfig | An existing policy configuration was updated, for example by adding, changing, or removing policy settings, or by changing the policy configuration's name, description, or scope. |

claims.where: Governance controls: Audit; What to check
claims.claim: UpdatedPolicyConfigPriority is the audit operation for a policy configuration priority change.
claims.quote: | Updated policy configuration priority | UpdatedPolicyConfigPriority | The priority of a policy configuration was changed. |

claims.where: Governance controls: To scope one group
claims.claim: Microsoft documents a two-configuration pattern with targeted users at priority 0 and All users at priority 1 using opposite Enabled and Disabled values.
claims.quote: Set the priority for Group A to a lower number (for example, priority 0) so it's evaluated before Group B (for example, priority 1). To do the reverse ... use the same two-group pattern with the Enabled and Disabled values swapped

claims.claim: The scope control is at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. On the Start with the basics page, enter a name ... On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for targeting a Cloud Policy configuration to groups.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Cloud Policy service API PowerShell create group policy configuration scope reorder priority'; '"Cloud Policy" "group-level" automation Graph'. Read Learn's overview-cloud-policy and graph/utcm-copilot-resources; no group-scoping API found; TCM supports tenant-level policies only.

claims.claim: Priority is controlled at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Reorder priority.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. To change the priority order for the policy configurations, select Reorder priority on the Policy configurations page.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API for reordering Cloud Policy configuration priority.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Cloud Policy" "Reorder priority" "API"'; '"Office Cloud Policy Service" API scope priority PowerShell'. Read overview-cloud-policy and TCM Copilot resources; results documented UI priority and unrelated Intune reorder operations, not an OCPS priority API.

claims.claim: The Pages and Notebooks setting is at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.
claims.quote: Select Customization from the left pane. Select Policy Management. Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one. From the Choose the scope dropdown list ... In Configure Settings ... Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the Pages and Notebooks baseline setting.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object that runs periodically ... to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode. mode ... Optional; defaults to monitorOnly.
claims.fix: Keep the method and path. Replace the row note with: 'Graph is beta and tenant-level only. Set mode to applyOnce; otherwise the call defaults to monitorOnly and does not apply the setting. In baseline.resources, use resourceType microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks and properties.value as the string "0" (disable) or "1" (enable).' The mode is documented at the API link and the resource properties at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-copilot-resources.

claims.claim: The baseline resourceType microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks uses the value property with allowed values 0 and 1.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks", "resourceVersion": 1, "properties": { "value": "1" }. 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting.

claims.claim: The code previews control is at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Enable code previews for AI-generated content in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages.
claims.quote: In Configure Settings, choose one of the following settings: ... Enable code previews for AI-generated content in Microsoft Copilot Chat and Copilot Pages ... Disabled: Copilot doesn't run code previews in Copilot Chat or Copilot Pages.

claims.claim: No code previews resource is listed in the TCM Copilot resource reference and no automation for this setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Cloud Policy Enable code previews AI-generated Copilot Chat Pages Graph API resource'; '"Enable code previews" "Graph"'. Read cpcn-admin-configuration; searched headings and code previews/codepreview in graph/utcm-copilot-resources; no matching resource or API found.

claims.where: What to check: audit search; Governance controls: Audit
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to search the Purview audit log, but the controls table has no audit-search row.
claims.quote: Search the Purview audit log for UpdatedPolicyConfig and UpdatedPolicyConfigPriority events after any change. No admin path or command for the audit search is a row here because it is Purview's.
claims.fix: Remove the final audit-search bullet from What to check, retaining the audit explanation and link to the auditing concept in Governance controls. This resolves the checklist/table mismatch without adding a control row.
